## Problem 1


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
T1 <- 100
N1.1 <- rep(NA, T1)
N1.1[1] <- 50
B1 <- D1 <- rep(NA, T1-1)
b1 <- 0.2
d1 <- 0.3
## They should repeat this 3 times. Several options for doing that.
set.seed(8934)
for(t in 2:T1) {
    B1[t-1] <- rpois(1, N1.1[t-1]*b1)
    D1[t-1] <- rbinom(1, N1.1[t-1], d1)
    N1.1[t] <- N1.1[t-1] + B1[t-1] - D1[t-1]
}
```
:::


We would need to set $b=d$ to acheive equilibrium.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
N1.2 <- rep(NA, T1)
N1.2[1] <- 50
B2 <- D2 <- rep(NA, T1-1)
b2 <- 0.3
d2 <- 0.3
for(t in 2:T1) {
    B2[t-1] <- rpois(1, N1.2[t-1]*b2)
    D2[t-1] <- rbinom(1, N1.2[t-1], d2)
    N1.2[t] <- N1.2[t-1] + B2[t-1] - D2[t-1]
}
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(1:T1, N1.1, type="o", ylim=c(0, 100),
     xlab="Time", ylab="Abundance")
lines(1:T1, N1.2, type="o", col=4)
```

## Problem 2




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
T2 <- 30                           ## time steps
n2 <- matrix(NA, nrow=3, ncol=T2)  ## age-class abundance matrix    
n2[,1] <- c(50, 40, 10)            ## abundance at t=1
s2 <- c(0.4, 0.5, 0.3)             ## survival rates
f2 <- c(0, 0.8, 1.7)               ## fecundities

A2 <- matrix(c(f2, s2[1], 0, 0, 0, s2[2], s2[3]), 
             nrow=3, ncol=3, byrow=TRUE)  
A2                                 ## Leslie matrix
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
     [,1] [,2] [,3]
[1,]  0.0  0.8  1.7
[2,]  0.4  0.0  0.0
[3,]  0.0  0.5  0.3
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
for(t in 2:T2) {
    ## Make the third fecundity random
    A2[1,3] <- rnorm(1, f2[3], 0.1)
    eps <- rnorm(3, 0, 0.5)
    n2[,t] <- A2 %*% n2[,t-1] + eps
}

matplot(1:T2, t(n2), type="l", ylim=c(0, 60),
        xlab="Time", ylab="Abundance")
legend(20, 60, paste("Age class", 1:3), col=1:3, lty=1:3)
```
